old: And compassionate toward distressed brahmins: the small gift that goes with faith reaches a boundless limit, O king; what is given, that one would not get from the twice-born.
new: Endowed with compassion toward distressed brahmins, and he who with faith reaches whatever small gift reaches a boundless limit, O king; what is given, that one would not get from the twice-born.
why: reviewer (error): dānam is accusative (the draft's own gram says n. acc. sg.) and object of upaiti, so it cannot be the subject. Also the printed ca stands after dayānvitaḥ, not at the start of the sentence.

old: Construction is loose and the sense of the whole is uncertain. The subject of the first upaiti is not stated: it can be the gift (dānam, as translated) or the compassionate person (dayānvitaḥ, nominative), in which case yat svalpam ... dānam would be 'whatever small gift he attains with faith'. yat ... dānam: yat may be the relative of dānam. dvijebhyaḥ (abl./dat. pl.) may be dative construed with dīyate ('what is given to the twice-born'); then labhet has no clear object. na labhet is translated literally. ananta-pāram: 'having no end as its limit'. The input has a double space between anantapāramupaiti and rājan and the line has only ten syllables; a word may be missing, no reading is proposed. The input has a double space between anantapāramupaiti and rājan and the line has only ten syllables; a word may be missing, no reading is proposed. The src of the token ' rājan' carries a leading space only so that the checker can reproduce the double space; the Sanskrit token is rājan.
